text1: A compact micro-rail built around a pair of tuning prongs. It flicks needles out in short pairs; every fourth needle is allowed to ring, and the chime spills over as an EMP arc that snaps at nearby missiles and fighters.
The ringing fourth shot of a Chime Repeater.
A needle-thin rail with a tensioned crystal at its breech. Left alone, the crystal stores its charge and the next slug leaves with a sharp, plucked report - and twice the bite.

Three short rails throw grown crystal shards in a near-parallel volley. Crude by Cantorate standards, the Shard Caster is what the lattice yards fit when a hull needs reach and has little flux to spare.

A lattice shard grown around a tuned core. It buries itself in the target's plating and hums there until an energy weapon strikes the same hull; the matching frequency shatters it from the inside. The lattice regrows spent spikes slowly.
Four Tuning Spike racks in an armored pod, for hulls that build their whole battle plan around the combo.

A long rail that tunes itself to whatever it keeps hitting. Every slug that lands on the same hull brings its resonance closer to the target's own, and the next one cuts deeper. Switching targets throws the tuning away.
A three-rail shard thrower. The flechettes are grown with fracture planes along their length, so a shard that lodges in plating keeps splitting - and cutting - for seconds after impact.
Three rails of different length, fired in sequence. Each note is driven harder than the last, and the third one lands like a struck bell.
Twin flak barrels that fire tuned fragmentation shells. The shells listen for missile drives and burst when the pitch is right.
The Cantorate's standard heavy gun: a fork of conductive rails that winds a lattice slug up to its breaking frequency and throws it across the battlefield. A clean hit on plating does not stop it.
The Conductor's spine is the gun. Its prongs wind the core crystal to a frequency no turret could survive.
A rapid heavy rail held on one note. Its slugs ring a shield at the pitch of the emitter's own dissipation band, and part of the load simply stays.
A slow torpedo carrying an unstable lattice bloom. On impact the bloom flowers outward as a ring of crystal fragments, and the shock arcs through anything nearby.
A crystal fragment of a Resonance Bloom.

The Virtuoso's voice. A long twin-rail lance that throws lattice slugs fast enough that nothing has time to move. Once a hull is bare, a slug goes straight through it and on into the next ship in line.
The Sforzando as the Unsung carries it: rails out of true, crystal dim. Still a fine gun. Not yet a voice.

A lattice dart barely larger than its own crystal. The Grace Note flips its core between two tunings in an instant: Harmonic, with the shield up and the seams running teal, or Discord, with the shield folded away, the seams burning violet and every weapon pushed past its rating.

In battle: a fast interceptor-frigate. Pitch Shift trades its shield for speed and damage; fit it to hunt frigates and finish cripples.

A stocky escort built around two hinged armor vanes. When the Refrain ties its core to an ally's, the vanes swing forward over its bow and a share of everything that hits the ally arrives on the Refrain's shield instead.

In battle: a fleet escort. Sympathetic Ward soaks part of an ally's damage on the Refrain's own shield. Built in: Escort Package.

A needle hull with forward-swept wings and a drive tuned for short, violent bursts. Its weapons leave fracture lines in whatever they hit, and enough of them make plating simply come apart.

In battle: a destroyer striker. Grace Dash in, unload, dash out; Fracture turns sustained hits into armor-shattering bursts. Built in: Fracture, Unstable Injector.

The Cantorate's line cruiser: an arrowhead with two accelerator rails swept back as barbs. Its Crescendo lets the energy batteries feed on their own rhythm, every hit quickening the next.

In battle: the line cruiser. Crescendo rewards keeping its energy guns on target. Built in: Dedicated Targeting Core.

Two narrow hulls joined by lattice girders, with real empty space between them. The Tremolo marks a point in space with a standing wave and can snap back to it, shedding the damage it took since.

In battle: a skirmishing cruiser. Standing Wave lets it commit hard and then snap back to safety, repairing part of what it lost. Built in: Auxiliary Thrusters.

A carrier threaded through a great ring that turns in a well at its heart. When the ring spins up, the space around the Fermata goes still: shots slow to a crawl and missile seekers lose their song.

In battle: a carrier that protects itself. Fermata Field slows incoming fire around it; Tuned Wings speeds up fighter replacement near the ship. Built in: Expanded Deck Crew, Hardened Subsystems.

A long steel blade split into two prongs with the Harmonic Driver set between them. The Conductor's core does not just resonate, it leads: every Lattice ship near it tunes to it, and what it marks, the whole chorus strikes.

In battle: the fleet flagship. Its spinal Harmonic Driver outranges almost anything, and Sympathetic Strike marks a target for every Lattice ship. Conductor's Bridge feeds the whole chorus Resonance. Built in: Stabilized Shields, Operations Center.

The Cantorate's lost first soloist, finished. A rapier of a capital with two Sforzando lances on its shoulders, a drive that skips across space and leaves a string behind it, and a core that feeds on the readiness of everything it wounds. At full voice, its seams burn gold.

In battle: a unique duelist capital. Glissando dashes through fire, the Sforzando lances skewer lines of ships, Stolen Time feeds on readiness and kills, and at 100% CR Bravura takes over. Built in: Concert Pitch, Auxiliary Thrusters.

A prototype that sang alone after its chorus died. The sash is bare metal, the lances are out of true and half the cells are dark, but it is still the fastest capital you have ever seen move, and it still takes what it needs from its enemies.

In battle: still a fast, dangerous capital, but untuned: no Bravura, one-third the skewer, a dimmer dash. Built in: Concert Pitch, Auxiliary Thrusters.

A lattice station: a crystal heart in a six-petal rosette, with a ring turning slowly around it. When a petal dies, its stored resonance floods the others.

In battle: a station of six petals. Grand Chorus fires from every petal at once; Phase-Locked Petals makes each loss strengthen the rest.
A lance petal of the Cantor Array.
A defensive petal of the Cantor Array, full of flak and point defense.
A hangar petal of the Cantor Array.
A needle interceptor with a micro-rail in its nose and canards for its tightest turns. Trills hunt fighters and missiles in pairs of notes, never far from the carrier that tuned them.
A heavy fighter built around twin rails. Cadenzas engage from well outside the range most fighters fight at, and keep plucking at a target until it breaks.
A rail bomber: one heavy slug that punches through armor and out the far side, and a pair of Tuning Spikes that the slug's own hits - or any Lattice energy weapon - will detonate.

Toggles the lattice core between two tunings.

Harmonic (off): shields available, +25% flux dissipation, and energy weapons add EMP damage.

Discord (on): shields locked off, +30% top speed and +20% weapon damage.

Overtone: switching tunings releases an EMP pulse.

A 720-unit blink-dash in the direction of movement; thrusting mid-dash bends its path. The ship cannot be hit while dashing. 2 charges (3 in Bravura).

Cost: 1% combat readiness per dash; unusable below 30%.

The String: the path stays behind as a taut string for 1.2 seconds. It deletes enemy projectiles that cross it, then snaps: 400 energy damage to every enemy touching it (fighters and missiles are destroyed) and 2% CR stolen from each ship hit.

For 2 seconds after a dash the Sforzando lances are Accented.

Overtone: the string snaps twice and the dash refunds half a charge.

Every petal discharges a synchronized resonant lance into the nearest enemy in its sector (600 energy damage each).

A small refugee polity in the pulsar system of Vell, descended from the staff of a Domain harmonic-flux laboratory that was cut off by the Collapse. The Cantorate builds its ships around crystalline lattice cores that lock to one another's pitch: a battle network with no comm traffic to jam and no AI core to ban.

Everything the Cantorate knows survives as scores, tuning protocols memorised by its engineers after the databanks were lost. Its crews hold their cores in tune through long shifts, its government rules by consensus, and dissent is treated as what it is in a choir: a fault that weakens everyone. Its first and oldest law is that no voice sings alone.

Poor in everything but crystal, the Cantorate cannot leave Vell, the only star whose beat its crystals grow true to. The Hegemony inspects its cores for artificial minds, Tri-Tachyon wants to buy or steal them, and the Luddic Path calls them machine-worship.

A neutron star that turns once every 1.3 seconds and sweeps the system with a beam of hard radiation. Its beat is steadier than any clock humanity has built, and it is the only reason anyone lives here: lattice crystal grows true only to a pulsar's rhythm.

A listening station in a tight orbit around Vell, shielded against the beam that crosses it every rotation. Tacet Station records the pulsar and broadcasts the Cantorate's reference pitch, the tone every lattice core in Vell is tuned against. Its archives hold what the refugees managed to save of the Antiphon Institute, and some of what they chose to forget.
A scorched rock that holds its orbit through the pulsar's beam. Nothing grows here and nobody has tried; the Cantorate's tuners use it as a reference target.
A cold, slow ice giant whose low radio drone gave it its name. Its moons are the Cantorate's home: Coda, where the refugees settled, and Glasshouse, where they grow the crystal.

A frozen moon of Basso and the capital of the Cantorate of Vell. Its habitats were dug by a refugee fleet that had run out of places to go, and they still hum: every district keeps a tuning shift, and the whole city falls silent at the change of watch.

Above it turns the Cantor Array, the largest lattice instrument the Cantorate has ever grown.

An airless moon of Basso where lattice crystal is grown in pressurised vaults timed to the pulsar. The nurseries are tended in shifts by workers who can hear a flawed crystal before any instrument can find it, and who lose that hearing young.
A lattice station of six petals around a crystal heart, turning slowly above Coda. When one petal is lost, its stored resonance floods the others.
A Domain-era listening buoy of the Antiphon Institute, left on the fringe to record the harmonic flux of hyperspace storms. Two centuries later some of them still listen.

The Antiphon Institute: a Domain hyperspace-physics laboratory, a spindle of dark habitat rings around a dock built for one capital ship. The Cantorate's ancestors fled it two centuries ago, and chose to forget where it was.
A Lattice hull of a pattern two centuries old, drifting in the abyss. Its crew are long dead. Its core still keeps time.
A Domain-era data cache of the Antiphon Institute, scored with five empty lines like a stave. Someone hid it here on purpose.
A cryogenic vault grown into a cold rock at the edge of the Sector, humming at the edge of hearing. On no chart.
A cold, airless rock circling a dim red star. Its only feature is the vault someone grew into it.
Where the First Chorus died. Lattice wrecks hang in a ring in the dark, and the abyss hums with them.
